conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Elena, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply a way to see how your mood, energy, and thoughts have been over the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting any support you might need. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell me you’re in immediate danger. We’ll go through ten questions; they’re pretty straightforward, and you can answer in your own words. When you’re ready, we can start.  

First question: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Hi, Elena… I guess I’ve laughed a little, maybe once or twice when my husband sent a silly meme, but mostly things don’t feel all that funny right now. Even when something should make me chuckle, it feels kind of muted—like I’m too tired or worried to really enjoy it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often. I can still chuckle if something is really funny, but most of the time the laughter just feels forced and fades fast.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even a shower without interruption—but lately it’s like I have to push myself to care. I still do them, hoping I’ll feel better, but the enjoyment is mostly gone. I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I do that a lot. If the baby won’t settle or I can’t get her to nap, I keep thinking it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not a good enough mom. Even when my husband says it’s normal, I still feel it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly imagine her choking, or I’ll check if she’s breathing a dozen times a night. Nothing specific sets it off—my mind just spins with “what-ifs,” and I can’t settle until I’ve triple-checked everything.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes, yeah. It’s like a tightness in my chest out of nowhere—like I’m bracing for something awful to happen, even when the room is quiet and the baby’s fine. It passes if I pace or distract myself, but it keeps creeping back.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, most days. It feels like the laundry, the feedings, the constant worrying—all of it—pile up faster than I can handle. I manage to get through the essentials, but I’m running on empty and snapping at little things that never used to bother me.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling through everything I might’ve messed up that day, or scary “what-ifs” about the baby. Some nights it takes me over an hour to drift off, and then I jolt awake at every tiny sound, checking the monitor again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the time, honestly. It’s like a heavy blanket I can’t shake off—I’ll be holding the baby and tears just well up for no clear reason. Some afternoons everything feels gray, and even when I tell myself I should feel grateful, the sadness is right there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Yeah, a few times this week. I’ll be folding onesies or just staring at the mess in the living room and suddenly I’m crying—quietly so no one hears. It’s not over anything big; it just spills out.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t felt that. I’m exhausted and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note**

**Patient-reported symptoms:**
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness, anhedonia
- Marked loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities
- Daily, unexplained anxiety and panic-like episodes (chest tightness, intrusive "what-ifs," repeated checking on infant)
- Excessive, inappropriate guilt/blames self when baby is fussy; doubts maternal competence
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems driven by ruminating worries
- Feeling overwhelmed, "running on empty," irritability

**Pattern:** Consistent with depressive and anxious distress emerging since delivery. No self-harm ideation reported.

**Screening significance:** Elevated scores for depressive and anxiety symptoms common in postpartum mood disorders; no current safety concerns.

**Next step:** Recommend formal clinical interview and use of standardized postpartum depression scale; consider referral for psychotherapy and/or medication evaluation as indicated.
